module_title: Advanced Analysis - Economic Indicators and Output Gaps
introduction: This advanced level focuses on the specific 'Indicators' economists use to predict the business cycle and the critical macroeconomic concept of the 'Output Gap'.

core_concepts.title: Leading Indicators
core_concepts.description: These are variables that change 'BEFORE' the overall economy changes. They predict the future phase of the business cycle. (Examples: The Stock Market, new orders for manufacturing goods, and building permits for new housing).

core_concepts.title: Lagging Indicators
core_concepts.description: These are variables that change 'AFTER' the economy has already entered a particular phase. They confirm the trend. (Examples: Unemployment Rate, Corporate Profits, and the Consumer Price Index / Inflation).

core_concepts.title: Coincident Indicators
core_concepts.description: These change 'AT THE SAME TIME' as the overall economy, providing a snapshot of the current state. (Examples: Current Real GDP, Index of Industrial Production (IIP), and Retail Sales).

core_concepts.title: The Output Gap
core_concepts.description:
This is the difference between a country's 'Actual GDP' and its 'Potential GDP' (what it could produce if 100% of its resources were fully employed). 
1. Negative Output Gap: The economy is underperforming its capacity (Recession / High Unemployment). 
2. Positive Output Gap: The economy is overworking its capacity (Unsustainable boom causing massive Inflation).

important_entities.title: Types of Business Cycles (By Duration)
important_entities.significance: 1. Kitchin Cycle: 3-5 years (Driven by changes in business inventories). 2. Juglar Cycle: 7-11 years (Driven by business investment in fixed capital). 3. Kuznets Cycle: 15-25 years (Driven by infrastructural and demographic changes). 4. Kondratiev Waves: 45-60 years (Driven by massive technological innovations like the Internet or Steam Engine).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In tough exams like UPSC, students logically assume that 'Unemployment' is a Leading indicator because it signals bad times. This is a TRAP. Companies do not fire workers immediately when demand drops; they wait until a recession is fully confirmed. Therefore, Unemployment is firmly a 'Lagging Indicator'.

exam_strategy_tips: 'What kind of indicator is the Stock Market?' is a highly repeated trivia question. Answer: It is a 'Leading Indicator' because investors buy/sell shares based on what they think the economy will do 6 months in the future.
